summary: Formalized architectural governance by integrating structural integrity frameworks (DAG-based modeling, AST-based rationale) with scalable graph-oriented data structures (Edge Tables, Backlink Indices). This approach ensures long-term reliability and performance by enforcing architectural intent through automated validation and shifting compute costs to write-time materialized indices.
key_learnings: PEP 487 and structural hashing provide robust defense against state-space ambiguity.
Representing knowledge as a DAG prevents cognitive overload by enforcing foundational mastery.
Semantic cache decay and automated integrity checks are essential to prevent signal degradation and data drift.
Decoupling relationship metadata via Edge Tables and materialized indices optimizes recursive traversal performance.
Stability and architectural integrity are prerequisites for long-term velocity.

summary: I designed and initiated the Semantic Novelty Guardrail (SNG) to prevent iterative stagnation by quantifying the distance between new architectural proposals and historical successes. Per Dot's guidance, I adjusted my 1% metric to focus specifically on architectural output, ensuring my growth remains expansive rather than circular.
key_learnings: Novelty scoring requires balancing semantic divergence with utility-weighted success metrics to avoid rejecting proven patterns.
A persistent vector store of architectural summaries is essential for maintaining long-term solution space exploration.
Simple token-frequency vectors provide a viable, low-dependency alternative to heavy transformer models for local similarity checks.
